definitions.explanation: describes someone who dislikes physical or mental effort; a person who is habitually lazy about doing things

examples.japanese: ものぐさな⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{直|なお}したい。
examples.english: I want to fix my lazy personality.

examples.japanese: ⟦{休日|きゅうじつ}→休日：03028_kyuujitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ものぐさになって⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{出|で}ない→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: On holidays, I become lazy and don't leave the house.

notes:
ものぐさ describes habitual laziness or an aversion to effort.

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧ (things) + くさい (to smell of, to seem like), suggesting "having the nature of avoiding things."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ものぐさな⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a lazy person)
- ものぐさな⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧ (a lazy personality)
- ものぐさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}め{込|こ}む→決め込む：13343_kimekomu⟧ (to deliberately be lazy)

USAGE:
- More about habitual reluctance to do things than pure laziness
- Often describes someone who avoids effort or tasks out of convenience
- Can have a mildly self-deprecating or humorous tone when used about oneself

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{怠|なま}け{者|もの}→怠け者：16970_namakemono⟧ (lazy person - more negative)
- {面倒|めんどう}くさ⟦がり→ガリ：27408_gari⟧ (someone who finds things troublesome)
- ⟦ぐうたら→ぐうたら：27861_guutara⟧ (slovenly, lazy - informal)
- {無精|ぶしょう} (lazy, indolent)

KANJI WRITING:
Can be written as {物臭|ものぐさ}, but hiragana is common.

REGISTER: Casual to neutral. Common in everyday speech.
